papers.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
papers.desc: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on instruction data can quietly erode their safety, even when no training example looks harmful.

papers.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
papers.desc: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control.

papers.title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
papers.desc: Real-world forgery is inherently heterogeneous: it manifests not only as digital manipulation but also as physical spoofing, and is carried not only by images but also by videos.

papers.title: When Requirements Interact: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding via Interdependent Specifications
papers.desc: To succeed in real-world long-horizon software development, coding agents must satisfy multi-dimensional task specifications, such as interface compatibility and error handling, and do so without breaking existing dependencies.

papers.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
papers.desc: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion.

papers.title: Supervising the Visible State: Separating Representation from View Selection in Streaming Video
papers.desc: An action seen once and the same action seen three times receive the same action-recognition label, so that supervision does not require a model to count.

papers.title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
papers.desc: An effective agent memory system should adapt to a user's history and task requirements.

papers.title: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding
papers.desc: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people.

papers.title: VoxLock: Target-Speaker Extraction for Voice Agents Without an Enrollment Step
papers.desc: A voice agent's speech recognizer transcribes everyone near the microphone, including people other than the caller.

papers.title: SciGame: Let Agents Play the Scientific Discovery Games in the Real and Counterfactual World
papers.desc: Large language model agents are increasingly used for scientific discovery.

papers.title: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report
papers.desc: Metis is a bet that better data, better training methods and new architectures can buy what a bigger parameter count cannot, at a fraction of the cost.

papers.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
papers.desc: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments.

papers.title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
papers.desc: Do research agents have taste, the judgment of which experiments are worth running before their outcomes are known? We give six frontier models seven recent NLP papers.

papers.title: AuditFL: A Contract-Backed Clearing Layer for Open Federated Learning
papers.desc: Federated learning (FL) keeps raw data local, but most deployments still rely on a trusted coordinator for client admission, checkpoint distribution, update collection, aggregation, and rewards.

papers.title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish
papers.desc: This paper presents TurnTurk-GPT, a text-based turn-taking predictor for Turkish obtained by fine-tuning a Turkish GPT-2 model with the TurnGPT objective on synthetic and real dialogue, and evaluates it on real Turkish conversation against rule baselines, a zero-shot Turkish language model and a widely used multilingual end-of-turn detector.
